track.why: Screens each commit: a Co-Authored-By trailer naming an AI assistant marks it as AI-written, which decides whether it is drilled when only AI-written commits count.

title: AI-written commits go unnoticed

sourceAnchors.explanation: The pattern for a Co-Authored-By trailer that names a coding assistant, and the check that applies it to a commit message.
Reads a commit's hash, parents, author email, subject and full message from git, and records whether an assistant co-authored it.

hints: Compare the commit that was picked up with the ones that were skipped: where in the message does the assistant line sit in each?
The pattern is anchored. Ask what that anchor matches in a message of several lines, and whether it can reach the last one.
regressionTestName: marks a Claude co-authored commit as AI-written
injectedBugDescription: The trailer pattern lost its multiline flag (/im became /i), so ^ only matches at the start of the whole message. A Co-Authored-By trailer is at the end of a multi-line message, so it is never found; a message that is only the trailer still matches. The regression test (and the readCommit test) use a full message with the trailer last.
